name: Czechia
tagline: The most beautiful city in central Europe, and a country that drinks more beer per head than any other.
summary: Bohemia and Moravia were the industrial heart of the Habsburg empire and came through the twentieth century with their architecture largely intact — Prague was not bombed. Outside it, spa towns, sandstone rock cities, Moravian vineyards and a chateau in every second valley go almost unvisited. Beer is a food group here and has been brewed in Plzeň since 1842.

season.note: Prague is busy from April to October and at Christmas. May and September are the best compromise. Winter is cold, cheap and atmospheric, and the beer halls are the point.

getting_around: Trains and buses are cheap, frequent and comfortable; RegioJet and České dráhy both serve the main routes. Prague's metro and trams are excellent and the night trams run all night.
food: Roast pork, dumplings and cabbage — vepřo knedlo zelo, the national plate
Svíčková: beef in a cream root-vegetable sauce with cranberry
Pilsner, drawn slowly with a thick head, at 4°C
know: Beer is often cheaper than water in a pub and ordering is done by putting a mat on the table.
The koruna, not the euro; card acceptance is near-universal in cities.
Prague's centre has aggressive currency-exchange scams — use a bank or an ATM from a real bank.

regions.name: Prague & Bohemia
regions.summary: The capital on its river, spa towns to the west, and sandstone rock towns to the north.

cities.name: Prague
cities.summary: Romanesque, gothic, baroque and cubist stacked on top of each other, with a castle above and a bridge in between.
highlights: Charles Bridge at six in the morning — genuinely worth the alarm
The castle complex and St Vitus's stained glass by Mucha
Vyšehrad, the other castle, with almost nobody on it
A pub where they draw a mlíko, a glass of pure foam, and mean it

experiences.name: A pub with a tapster, not a menu
experiences.summary: The good places pour continuously and mark your tab in pencil; you say when to stop, and the pour type is a real choice.

experiences.name: Vyšehrad and the river bend
experiences.summary: The city's first castle, a cemetery of composers, and the whole of Prague from the ramparts without a crowd.

cities.name: Český Krumlov
cities.summary: A castle town in a tight loop of the Vltava, essentially unchanged since the 18th century.
highlights: The baroque theatre, with original 1766 machinery still working
The bear moat, which has had bears since the 1700s
Canoeing the river loop around the town

cities.name: Český ráj (Turnov)
cities.summary: 'Bohemian Paradise': sandstone towers, rock cities and castles on pinnacles, ninety minutes from Prague.
highlights: Prachovské skály's maze of rock corridors
Trosky castle on two volcanic plugs
Sandstone climbing where the rules ban metal protection

regions.name: Moravia
regions.summary: The eastern half: vineyards, an astronomical clock nobody queues for, and a functionalist villa that changed architecture.

cities.name: Brno
cities.summary: Czechia's second city: student, modernist and self-deprecating, with an ossuary of 50,000 under the square.
highlights: Villa Tugendhat, Mies van der Rohe, 1930, bookable in advance only
The second-largest ossuary in Europe, found in 2001
A cannonball fired at 11 am, which is why the cathedral rings noon an hour early

cities.name: Mikulov
cities.summary: A chateau town on the Austrian border, surrounded by the country's best vineyards and a limestone ridge.
highlights: Wine cellars cut into the rock, open at harvest
The Jewish quarter and cemetery, one of central Europe's most important
Pálava's limestone hills and their orchids

experiences.name: A Moravian cellar at harvest
experiences.summary: Burčák — half-fermented, cloudy and briefly available each September — is drunk cold from the barrel and does not travel.
